Clara Nguyen: Quick sync 12 we need a consistent mapping from internal route/quota codes to client-facing messages + console badges. Support is seeing too many ambiguous tickets.
Bryan Lee: Yep. What's the minimal set of buckets you want?
Clara Nguyen: Leaning to three consumer-facing buckets: `retryable-backoff` (transient capacity; include retry hint), `rate-limited` (hard quota / billing surface), and `degraded` (serving a fallback or lower-quality model). Console badges + telemetry should reflect those exact words.
Sara Patel: That makes sense. small nuance: some soft-throttles should show as `degraded` for a short window to make impact visible in console, even if the route is technically still accepting requests.
Alex Kim: Current internal codes: `ROUTE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `SOFT_THROTTLE`, `FALLBACK_VARIANT`, `MODEL_DEGRADED`. Do we keep those and add a new field `client_bucket`?
Clara Nguyen: Proposal: keep all internal codes for ops/debugging. Add `client_facing_bucket` (string) and `client_hint` (short human message <=120 chars) in the API error payload. SDKs will surface `client_hint` and `Retry-After` header when present.
Bryan Lee: SDK UX: map `client_facing_bucket` -> UI affordance. Example: `degraded` => small banner; `retryable-backoff` => snackbar with retry timer. Also emit `client_bucket` telemetry tag server-side for dashboards.
Sara Patel: Telemetry fields we should emit: `client_bucket`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `quota_window`, `fallback_variant`. That lets SRE/product pivot graphs by tenant and route.
Alex Kim: For dashboards we should surface a one-line sampled reason for top incidents (e.g., "Quota burst from long-running batch job"). We can sample `client_hint` plus ops annotations for that.
Clara Nguyen: Ops workflow idea: if a route has >5% calls in `retryable-backoff` for 5m, auto-open an issue and mark route as `attenuated` in Console. Need thresholds in runbook.
Sara Patel: Runbook: clarify tenant-level quota vs route-level rate limits handling. Console badges: `softly degraded` (yellow), `rate limited` (red), `fallback active` (purple). We'll include keyboard-hover copy and a link to the runbook.
Bryan Lee: Suggested API response example: `{ "error_code": "429", "internal_code": "ROUTE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED", "client_facing_bucket": "rate-limited", "client_hint": "Request quota exceeded for this route. Retry after 60s or contact billing." }`
Alex Kim: Also add header `X-RW-Client-Bucket: rate-limited` for easy log detection.
Sara Patel: Metrics plan: emit counter `client_bucket.count` and histogram `client_bucket.latency_impact` so product can correlate quality vs cost.
Bryan Lee: Rollout plan: opt-in org flag + additive optional fields so older clients ignore them. Canary on Dedicated with 10 orgs, then expand to Hosted.
Clara Nguyen: Timeline: Week1 design + API prototype + SDK stubs. Week2 canary (10 orgs). Week3 console badges + alerting. Week4 full launch.
Alex Kim: SDK mapping notes: surface `client_hint` as `error.humanMessage` and keep `error.internalCode` unchanged. Add unit/e2e tests: simulate `SOFT_THROTTLE` -> verify header + message surfaced.
Sara Patel: Design copy for console glossary: `retryable-backoff` -> "Temporary capacity issue; please retry later."; `rate-limited` -> "Request limit reached; consider upgrading or contact support."; `degraded` -> "Using lower-quality fallback to preserve availability."
Bryan Lee: thumbs up on copy. ops-bot: created checklist #8472 for runbook and alerts.
Clara Nguyen: Action items: Bryan = API schema + headers; Sara = runbook + badge art + copy; Alex = SDK mapping + tests; I'll own telemetry tags and canary cohort.
Bryan Lee: I'll open PRs today for schema and the feature flag `client_bucket_release`.
Sara Patel: I'll add design tickets and ping legal re: billing language.
Alex Kim: Adding SDK tests and backwards compatibility checks. Will add an e2e that forces `SOFT_THROTTLE` and asserts header + message.
Clara Nguyen: Final caveat: do not repurpose existing internal codes. Map them to buckets in the routing layer instead.
Bryan Lee: Sounds good. Any objections?
Sara Patel: None. :+1:
Alex Kim: None.
Clara Nguyen: Great. I'll write a short RFC and attach the mock API schema. Thanks everyone.
